blocks.en: Let $\Omega$ be an open, locally Jordan measurable set in $\mathbb{R}^m$. The dual space of $L^1(\Omega)$ is denoted by $L^\infty(\Omega)$.
blocks.zh: 设 $\Omega$ 为 $\mathbb{R}^m$ 中的局部 Jordan 可测开集. $L^1(\Omega)$ 的对偶空间记为 $L^\infty(\Omega)$.
blocks.label: def:lp-infinity-dual-space

source_locations.bbox_precision: visually selected parent block, top-left PDF points

blocks.en: Since test functions are dense in $L^1(\Omega)$, and convergence in the sense of test functions implies $L^1$-convergence, $L^\infty(\Omega)$ is a space of distributions. Moreover, since a uniform limit of continuous functions is also continuous, continuous functions cannot be dense in $L^\infty(\Omega)$; in fact, $L^\infty(\Omega)$ is not separable. In measure theory, $L^\infty$ is characterized as the space of bounded measurable functions.
blocks.zh: 由于试验函数在 $L^1(\Omega)$ 中稠密, 且试验函数意义下的收敛蕴含 $L^1$ 收敛, $L^\infty(\Omega)$ 是一个分布空间. 此外, 由于连续函数的一致极限仍连续, 连续函数不可能在 $L^\infty(\Omega)$ 中稠密; 事实上, $L^\infty(\Omega)$ 不可分. 在测度论中, $L^\infty$ 被刻画为有界可测函数的空间.
